utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Gopalan, I hear there's been some success with the exhibits.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm told 15 that are to be marked for identification are to be admitted, 50 public documents are to be admitted by consent, and 3 admitted by consent but under seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: If those figures are right, there will be a general order that the court officer will process those and will issue a memorandum with the exhibit numbers.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Does that save you a lot of reading.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Indeed. [Trial Chamber and registrar confer].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: What I said was ambiguous. The 15 marked for identification will be marked for identification, not admitted as exhibits.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: I believe they are part of the motion to add exhibits.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. Now, ready for the next witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Yes, I am, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Djurdjic, you've got some of yours agreed to. 12, is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. First of all, I would like to notify you that in the end I accepted all the documents of the Prosecution, and they failed to note that. So regardless of whether they are the police documents or not, I accepted them because I believe that in this trial if there is no doubt about a document, we need to have them and exhibit them and show them to the witness so that they explain to us what this is all about. And we will at one point come to a stage where we will be able to do that outside of the trial itself, the hearing itself. The Prosecution agreed with the list of documents that we submitted to the court deputy, and I would like to move that those Defence documents that the Prosecution has not objected to also be admitted into evidence. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Those documents will also be admitted and there will be a memorandum published by the court officer indicating the exhibit numbers. Now, after the slow pace of the last witness for good reason, we hope we can have a couple of quick-pace witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Would you please read aloud the affirmation which is shown to you now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I declare that I shall say truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, please sit down. Ms. Gopalan has some questions for you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Before we begin, I would just like to check if you've got your spectacles with you this morning, because we may be needing it in the course of the proceedings. That's wonderful.

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Please could you state your full name for the record.

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: Sami Parashumti.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. And how old are you?

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Sir, where were you born?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: I was born on the 13th of August, 1955, in Gjakove.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And where do you live now, sir?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: I still live in Gjakove.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd now like to ask you some questions about your statements. Now, do you recall that you gave a statement to members of this Tribunal on the 30th of January, 2000?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Sir, have you recently had the opportunity to review the statement?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Sir, I understand that having reviewed the statement, you wish to make some corrections to it?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: I will now take you through the corrections and if you could let me know if you agree with the corrections. Let's begin. In the English page 2, paragraph 3, the B/C/S is the same reference.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And for the Court's information, this is 65 ter 05182.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: You say: "I observed the home of Dardan Riza being set on fire." The correction you wish to make is as follows: "I saw flames from Dardan Riza's house. I learned from one of my neighbours that Dardan Riza's house had been set on fire." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. If we can correct the statement in this manner, well, then, I think that the witness is the one who should do it, not the Prosecution. If the correction is not made in the course of the evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: This is a matter of form rather than substance, Mr. Djurdjic. The witness is in his evidence agreeing to these changes, and it saves time if the matter is not obviously contentious. We'll proceed on that basis. Carry on, please, Ms. Gopalan.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Sir, I'll take you to the second correction wish to make to your statement that is page 3, paragraph 2, of both the English and the B/C/S. The 7th sentence. Currently your statement reads: "I noticed two dark blue armoured vehicles parked near the Vejsa home and also four dark blue jeeps parked around the corner near the store." The correction you wish to make is as follows, and I'll read it out now: "I noticed one dark blue armoured vehicle parked near the Vejsa home, and I heard the noises of other vehicles. I later learned from my neighbours that there were also four dark blue jeeps." Is that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: Yes, it is true that I only saw one. The other neighbours saw the others. However, I did hear the noise of the engines, of the other cars, that is.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. And finally, you wish to highlight another correction that you made to the statement, that's statement of the 30th of January, 2000. And this correction is already set out in your supplemental statement of the 15th of March, 2002. This is also part of 65 ter 05182. And I will just read out the correction that you made in your statement of March 2002: "Because of the darkness and my state of fear, I am not sure that the two policemen, Dragan Shipanoviq and Nenad Raqeviq whom I mentioned in my statement really were present, but I suspect it was them." That's the end of the correction.

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: Yes, it is correct, and true.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Now, having made these corrections to your statement of January, 2000, sir, one of which is set out in your supplemental statement of March 2002, are you satisfied that both these statements are true and accurate to the best of your knowledge and belief?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: Yes, they are.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I seek to tender this exhibit into evidence; it's 05182.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be assigned P00903, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: I will now read out the witness's in-court summary. The witness is a Kosovo Albanian male who lived in Millosh Giliq in Djakovica in 1999. The witness will testify that on the 2nd of April around midnight he saw Serb police knocking on doors along Millosh Giliq street. He saw smoke rising from the Riza house and subsequently learned from a neighbour that it had been set on fire. He also heard gun-shots from the area of the Vejsa family residence and children screaming "they are going to kill us." Approximately 15 minutes later, he heard more gun-fire coming from the Vejsa house. The witness escaped to the roof of his house and saw flames from the homes that were on fire. From that vantage point, he also observed 12 policemen in his yard, and he describes the uniforms of those policemen. He also saw approximately 50 policemen along the street and one dark blue armoured vehicle parked near the Vejsa home. The witness will testify that he saw policemen coming out of the Cana house with Januz Cana's daughter, Shpresa. He saw them take her into a tunnel by the house. He saw that one policeman had a knife, and shortly after he heard Shpresa scream. The witness then saw his house was on fire and fled to nearby houses. He then joined a convoy heading to Albania with his family and crossed the border into Albania. That's the end of the summary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Sir, I now have a few questions for you about the events on these early hours of the 2nd of April. Sir, in your statement, you say - and this is at page 2, paragraph 3 of the English, and the B/C/S is the same reference - you say that on the 2nd of April, at approximately 12.05 a.m., the Serb police started knocking on doors along Milosh Gilic Street. Sir, how did you know that these were policemen, those that were knocking on the doors?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: Yes, one could hear the noise of the doors. Some doors were iron doors others were wooden so that when the doors opened a lot of noise could be heard. And we were able to conclude that attacks against us were beginning. It was a very quiet night and even the lightest of the noises could easily be heard. And so this started coming from the other houses to our own because we happened to be in the corner at the end of the street.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Now, let's go back to the question. How did you know that those who were knocking on the doors were policemen?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: I know because when I was sitting on the roof-top and trying to assess which way I'd be able to make my escape without the presence of policemen, I was able to see near a corner a car that had stopped and policemen emerging from it. Some were hiding behind, others were almost in the courtyard of Xhemil Caka's house. They had weapons, and they were leaning against fences and giving commands right left and centre as to which way people were to go.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Let me just stop you there to clarify what you have said, but before we move on to you being on the roof, I'd like to take you back to when you were in Januz Cana's home, and this was after the police started knocking on the doors. I'd like to ask you some questions about Januz Cana. Who was Januz Cana?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: Januz Cana was one of our neighbours, next-door neighbours. My house and his house are adjacent.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. And you say that while you were standing by Januz Cana's front door, you heard gun-shots coming from the area of the Vejsa family residence, which is located across the street. This is paragraph 3 of the English, page 2, and the same in the B/C/S. I'd like you to identify --

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: -- some of the homes that you have mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Could I call up 65 ter 275, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Sir, shortly there should be a photograph appearing on your screen. Sir, do you recognise this photograph?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: Yes, I do. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: What does this photograph depict?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: This photograph shows the Vejsa family house from above.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: I will ask you, if you can, to mark on the photograph the Vejsa family home, and the usher will assist you with this. Could you please put the letter A beside the Vejsa family home, and circle the Vejsa home, please.

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. And could you please put the letter B beside your own home or on your own home.

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: My house.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And could you please put a letter C on the Cana home, please.

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd like to tender this document into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Sir, in your statement you say after you returned to your home -- oh, sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: And that will be assigned P00904, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Sir, you say approximately 15 minutes later - and this is at paragraph 3 of the English, page 2, and B/C/S page 2, paragraph 3, so the same reference - you say you heard a second burst of gun-fire coming from the Vejsa home. Now, you've just marked the Vejsa home for us on the map. Could you tell us, did you learn what was the -- what happened in the Vejsa home on that day?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: We learned of it when we were in Albania that there were about members of four families who died. We didn't see anything when we were there. All we heard was the gun-shots. And they say that the first of the attacks was the shop and Hisen Gashi was killed in his courtyard and then uninterrupted gun-fire could be heard in the areas as well as the screams of women and children. And after the uninterrupted burst of gun-fire, no more noises could be heard. No one was alive.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, I'd now like to move on to what you saw from the roof. You mentioned this earlier. In your statement you say: After hearing the Serbs trying to enter the Cana house, you tried to escape by proceeding to the roof of your house. Could you tell us what you saw from the roof of your house?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: With my own eyes -- may I make a point, references to where I was and what kind of vantage point I had?

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Yes, you may. If you could mark with a D where you were on the roof of your house.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Perhaps we could call up P275 -- sorry, 65 ter 275 again, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Could you mark for us, sir, where you were on the roof.

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the previous document we admitted, I believe the witness already drew this roof D, and he is now again drawing it on the new document. Because when he said "may I," he was told he may, but perhaps we should check. I believe there's another D already on that document. Maybe we'll have a surplus.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I only saw A, B, and C, Mr. Djurdjic. But if it's marked twice, it doesn't matter. Carry on, please, Ms. Gopalan.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Now, from the point that you marked now on this photograph, please tell us what you saw.

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: There was a police van, a blue one, here. May I mark where it was?

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Not for the moment, please. Could you just tell us what you saw after you saw the police van.

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: The van stopped, the lights were off, and the policemen came out.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Now, in your statement you say that you saw or you observed 12 policemen in your yard and that some of them were wearing blue camouflage. And this is at the English page 2, paragraph 4. B/C/S pages 2 to 3, also paragraph 4 for page 2. Now, sir, what were the rest of the policemen wearing? You said some were wearing blue camouflage, what were the rest wearing?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: Three of them were wearing blue uniforms. Oh, I'm sorry, they were wearing green uniforms. Three of them. While the other ones were all wearing blue uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Are these the policemen who you observed in your yard, the men that you have just described?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: Yes. These three in green uniforms were in my own yard. The other ones went close to our wall, but they were looking towards the Cana family home. They wanted to climb the wall or what they wanted to do, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: I'd like to tender the markings on the screen into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It's merely the D.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: That's right, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You don't want the position of the vehicle?

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: I could ask the witness to identify the vehicle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Sir, early on, you mentioned that you saw a police vehicle. Could you mark for us with an E where that vehicle was located, please.

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: I'd now like to tender the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And I'd like to call up P831, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: And the marked version, Your Honours, will be assigned P00905.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Sir, shortly on your screen there will appear some patterns of uniforms, and I'd like you to tell us, if you can, if any of those patterns were similar or the same to what you saw the policemen you mentioned wearing.

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: As far as I remember -- may I write the number of the ones that I saw?

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: If you could just identify them for us. There are four samples there. There's one on the top left-hand corner, top right-hand corner, bottom left, and bottom right. If it's easier, you can also mark the ones that you saw with a tick or some sort of marking.

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: There were three wearing this kind of uniform. There were 12 wearing this one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. For the record, the witness has marked the top right with a horizontal dash and a number 3 in the margin next to it, and has marked the top left pattern with a dash and the number 12 in the margin next to it.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Sir, where did you see these policemen?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: I saw all of them. I think I made a mistake earlier. There were 12 altogether, and 3 of them who were wearing green uniforms were in my own yard. And there were 9 wearing the blue uniforms. Earlier I made a mistake, the total number was 12.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: In that case, could you scrub off, you could cancel off the 12, and replace it with I think what you have said is that you saw 9 of them wearing the blue uniforms.

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. You also say in your statement that you saw another 50 policemen on the street. And this is at page 3, paragraph 2, English and B/C/S is the same reference. Now, what were they wearing, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: All of them were wearing this colour.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Let the record indicate that the witness has marked the top left-hand corner camouflage pattern.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. And what were these policemen doing?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: They were far away from where I was staying at the Caka family home; but I could hear that orders were being given, and they were leaning against the fence. There was a wire fence and they were giving orders left and right. I couldn't hear the voices there, but I could hear the voices of the people who were closer to my home, and I could hear that they were speaking in Serbian and also in Russian. There was a language I could not understand. I mean, spoken by the people who were close to where I was. I was -- they were right in front of the balcony about a couple of metres from my balcony. That's where the 12 were. And then I could see that more policemen were coming close to the Caka family home. They were about 50. I'm not sure exactly how many, maybe 45 or 50, but I could see them.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Sir, just going back to your answer when you say that you could hear orders being given and they were leaning against the fence, did you see --

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: Just a second, please. I've got a problem. [In English] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Let me just repeat my question, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Just going back to the answer that you gave earlier that you heard orders being given, do you remember what orders they were?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: I can hardly remember. I could hear people saying things: go left, go right, go to this house, or go to this direction, and search the houses.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: I'd like to tender this exhibit into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And I'd like to call up P318, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Sir, early on, you marked for us -- I'll wait.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: And the marked version, Your Honours, will be assigned P00906.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd now like to call up P318, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Sir, earlier on in your testimony you marked for us and you mentioned of a vehicle that you saw. Do you remember that, a vehicle that you saw by the Vejsa home? Now, on your screen there are photographs of a number of vehicles. If you are able to identify any of these vehicles as the one that you saw by the Vejsa family home, please let us know which number that is. Now, on page 1 there are four photographs. Did you see any of these vehicles by the Vejsa family home?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: I did not see these ones.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Let's move on to the second page then --

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: I did not see them near the Vejsa home only.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Could we have the second page, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. May I mark?

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: If you could just read out the number for us, please.

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: Number 7. But not in this colour. It was blue, the police colour.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. I'd now like to move on to when you left your home. You say at page 3, paragraph, 5 of the English: "I noticed that my house was on fire and that I had better leave." 1

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: The B/C/S is pages 3 to 4 beginning with paragraph 4.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And then you also say that around 7.00 a.m. those in the Krasniqi home including yourself departed for Albania. Sir, how many of you were gathered in the Krasniqi home?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: There were about 300 of us. 300, even more. I'm sure about 300 though.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. And, sir, you then say that you departed for Albania. Why is it that you departed for Albania?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: We departed because both on the right-hand side and left-hand side of the neighbourhood all the houses were burned. We did not have anywhere to stay, only the Serb houses were not burned. And some of the Albanian houses were not burned because they were next to the Serb houses, and if they had burned the Albanian houses, then the Serbs would have suffered as well. And there was nothing else for us to do but leave the neighbourhood because there was this foul smell. I can't describe it to you what kind of smell it was. Horrible.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And, sir, you mentioned houses being burned. Do you know who burnt these houses?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: Their houses -- these houses were burned by the people who entered the yards. There was nobody else to burn them.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Now, during your journey to Albania, what, if anything, happened to your identity documents?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: Yes. When we left the neighbourhood and were on our way to Albania, Besim Bokshi was leading the way; he was the first in the convoy and we followed him. We went along the Dan Leshi Street and then went to the Main Street close to the courthouse. Behind me there were about 200 or 300 people, and a bus attacked us, a bus of the Lasta company.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Just because I'm running out of time, I'd just like to take you to my question early on where I asked what, if anything, happened to your identity documents. Did anything happen to your identity documents?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: I did have my ID card, and I handed it over. On the outskirts of town there are two bridges, the old and the new one. At the old bridge, there was -- there were three policemen, and we had to show the ID card to them and then we had to drop it on the ground. After that, we had the right to proceed towards Albania.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. And what about the others who were in your group, what happened to their identity cards or other identity documents?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: Everybody was asked to show their ID cards. The ones that did not have their IDs were stopped there. I don't know what happened to them because we continued on our way to Albania.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Sir, could you tell us which route you took to Albania? What towns did you pass?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: Yes. After we passed the Tabako [phoen] bridge, we went to Brekoc. This is an outlying village. The second village is Vugova. The third one Zhubi. At Zhubi, the army was stopping the refugees and loaded them on tractors to go towards Albania. We were not able to walk after Zhubi; we had to get on tractors and go to the border. When we got to the border, the elderly men and women that were there were helped by the Yugoslav Army. They were taken towards the Albanian border. The disabled people, the sick and elderly, were helped by the army.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Now, you mentioned refugees in Zub. Do you remember how many refugees there were in Zub?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: When we got there we found about 250 of them there. When our convoy got there, there were about 800 altogether. There were other convoys coming from elsewhere, from other directions. I could not see the end of the convoy, but there were a large number of people, about 800. And then we were told to get on tractors in groups and we were directed towards Albania and the Albanian border.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And in which town or at which point did you cross over into the Albanian border, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: We crossed at Qafa e Prushit through the mountains, because the main road where the customs offices of Albania and Yugoslavia were had been mined, so the army directed us towards this other road and to the border there.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Just to finish off, I'd like to go back to your return to Djakovo. You've already spoken a little bit about this. Could you tell us, if you remember, when it is that you returned from Albania back to your neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: I returned to my neighbourhood in Gjakove on the 25th of June, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: I'd now like to call up 65 ter 275 again, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Sir, you've already mentioned the -- what you smelled when you returned to your neighbourhood and the condition of some of the homes. You said that homes had been burned but some homes -- you also said that some homes had not been burned, Albanian homes, because they were adjacent to Serb homes. Now, in this picture that you've already seen, could you mark for us -- could you circle the homes that were not burned?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Could the usher please assist.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: If you could just circle the homes that were not burned.

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: The Serb houses that were not burned, you want me to mark them, to put a circle?

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: This is Xhemil Caka's house and -- or Dan Caka's house. This one was not burned.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Sir, could you put a circle around the Serb houses that were not burned. I know that you've put a marking, but I am afraid it's not clear.

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: Like this?

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. And whose house was that?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: The first one was the house of an elderly Serb woman. Her children were living in Serbia; I don't know what town. She was living there on her own.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Could you put a number 1 beside that house, please. This house that you mentioned belonging to the elderly Serb woman.

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: Number 1.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. And how about the second circle --

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: There was another one that belonged to a Montenegrin. This one here. Mat Buriqi's house.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: You marked that house with a number 1, but I'd like you to put a number 2, please, Mat Buriqi's house.

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: Here, number 2.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And how about the circle in the middle that you haven't given a number to, who did that house belong to?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: This is Xhemil Caka's house, and this other one --

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: What was his ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: Albanian.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: From the photograph it appears that his house was not burned, do you know why that's the case?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: Xhemil Caka's house was not burned because it was next to the Serb woman's house, and it would burn if the Albanian's home would burn.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: This other house belonged to Ketar Kastrati and that house was not burned as well because it was next to the Montenegrin's house.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you, sir --

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: Next to house number 2.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Before we finish, could you please put a number 3 on Xhemil Caka's house.

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: That's it.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Sir, at this stage I have no further questions for you. I'd like to tender this document into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: And that will be assigned P00907, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Gopalan. Mr. Djurdjic, are you now ready to cross-examine? Would you like a break now or are you able to continue?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Parashumpti, my name is Veljko Djurdjic, and I'm a member of the Defence team representing the accused Vlastimir Djordjevic. And I am here in the courtroom with Ms. Marie O'Leary who is also a member of the Defence team. Are you feeling okay?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now I would like us to continue in the same vein as you did with Ms. Gopalan. I would like you to look at the transcript and when you see that the cursor has come to a stop, then please start answering the question, because I speak rather fast. Mr. Parashumti, you were born in Djakovica, was your father also born in Djakovica?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And in 1999, who were you living with in the house that you showed us?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: I live in a flat. It's 54 square metres all in all. Before the 24th of March, somewhere around the 20th, I returned to my parents' house because of the fear that on account of about 50 per cent of Serbs living in the neighbourhood, I would not feel quite safe.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And could you tell me who did you -- who were you with when you came to your parents' house?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: We split in two groups. My wife, my second daughter, and the little son went by the in-laws. Me and my eldest daughter and my biggest son went to my parents, and this because we were afraid to be all together. At least if one lot were to be killed, at least the others would survive. This was our thinking. She stayed at the in-laws for three days and then she returned with the two children where we stayed at my parents house, from her own parents house, and we stayed there until the 2nd of April when we departed to Albania.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And could you tell me who lived in your parents' house when you came in March 1999?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: My father who died two years ago, my mother who died a year ago, my brother, and his wife. Four people altogether.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. How many brothers did you have, brothers who were alive, in March 1999?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: We are four brothers. Two of us live abroad and two have lived in the Gjakove city.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And you are one of the two that lived in Djakovica?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, can you tell me whether the two brothers who were abroad remained there during the war in 1999?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: Yes, one has been living abroad for 38 years. The other brother used to live there and he returned two years -- he had left Kosova two years earlier, and he was there during the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Abroad?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Whenever you can, please answer by just saying yes or no. And I see here that you said that you had four or five children. Could you please tell me what -- how old were they in 1999?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: I have four children. I never said I had five. I have four. Two daughters and two sons. The eldest daughter was 16. The second daughter was 15. My eldest son was 13. And the little son was 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Parashumti, I can see that you did your national service. What colour uniform did you wear when you were in the army?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: Blue. It was the colour of the army, and I served my military service in Slovenia.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Were you perhaps in the border patrol?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: No, I was a driver. I had my instruction to Rijeka, but the appointment was given to me at Tulmin near Nova Gorica.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And can you tell me whether you served in the reserve force once you returned from your national service in the army?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And did you have any insignia on the uniforms, and if yes, what kind of insignia?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: Yes. Can you please repeat because I did not quite understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I asked you if you had any kind of insignia on the uniform, or if you didn't, perhaps if other people did, if they had some rank that you didn't have?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: Do you mean my uniform or somebody else's uniform? My uniform was the simple soldier's uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And did the officers have any kind of insignia on their uniforms; and if yes, do you remember what kind of insignia and where were they?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember. And even asking about that could lead us into who we were and what kind of soldiers they had. Vukusic, Mario, who was mine and my platoon's commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Do you understand what I'm asking you? I'm asking you whether the commander of whatever platoon, company, battalion, had any insignia; and if you do, what kind of insignia, do you remember that? I'm not interested in the persons names.

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: The commander was a four-star rank officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you tell me where was your apartment in Djakovica? What street?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: My apartment?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: At the outskirts of the town way out of the city on the way to Prizren near the police station. There is a building which is called Skenderbeu number 12.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And can you tell me how far is it from your parents' house, that apartment?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: About 5 kilometres, 4 and a half, 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And could you tell me how long had you lived in that apartment of yours?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: I got into that place in 1989, and I still live there, after this year that is, 2009.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And can you tell me, your wife and your two children went to her parents place, is this in the same area, in the Milosh Gilic Street or was it in some other neighbourhood in Djakovica?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: My wife went to Cabrat. It's a neighbourhood which is called the Qyli neighbourhood which from the main road takes you to Cabrat.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And where was Afrim Berisha's house?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: Afrim Berisha's house was behind mine, about 35 metres away. There is an empty space, like a road, there's the wall and then it's his house. So it's behind me and Januz Cana's houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell me your parents' house, where was the entrance to the house, on what side? I mean, what side of the street, were they from Milos Gilic Street or some other street?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: There were two entrances because we lived with our uncle as well, so he had his own entrance and we had ours on the side, on the Fehme Agani side of the street. We also had two back entrances, my uncle's as well as ours. The doors were smaller, though. They are not the same size as the front doors on the Fehme Agani side of the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And in 1999 was the street called Fehme Agani Street, or did it have some other name?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: Forgive me, it was called Millosh Giliq at that time. It is now called Fehme Agani. I suddenly confused the two eras. But in the old days it was certainly called Millosh Giliq.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell me -- well, I saw on the photograph the first house from the street, was it your brother's house and then your house was behind it, or were the two houses side by side?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: My uncle's house and my house shared the same roofs. It was the same big house split in two, which is the same to this day. We haven't finished --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Sorry, I got mixed -- I got mixed up. Could you please just tell me whether they were deeper into the courtyard, or were they on the street itself?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: They were deeper. There was a yard in front.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You must know how wide and how deep this plot of land was?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: It's about 5 acres altogether. I think it's 14 metres wide; I don't know how deep it is though, but I know that the surface area is about 5 acres.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And could you tell me, from the street, from the gate at the entrance to the yard and -- how far was it from the house? So from the street to the house, what was the distance?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: I understand, I understand. About 20 metres, but I can't be certain. It could be 22, it could be 23; I'm not certain.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course you can't. I'm asking you to give me an approximation. And the yard itself, was there a wall around it?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: On two sides of the house there was wall. However, between my uncle's house and ours, we had a gate.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And how high was the wall and what was the wall made of?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: It was built of building blocks, concrete. The height, I don't understand. Do you mean how high it was, the wall?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: I think roughly 1.60 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And the gate, what was it made and how high was it?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: The doors at my place and the uncle's place were iron made. It was at a distance of 22, 23 metres up to the balcony of the house. I could be wrong by roughly 2 or 3 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And could you please describe the house where you were. What did the house look like?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: Just like a normal house, a one-storied house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that it had a ground floor and then the first floor, and that's all?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: One story, it had a single roof.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And could you tell me how high the house was? How high could you get, for instance?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: Do you mean the wall or do you mean the entire height of the house?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Not the height of the house. I mean the height from the ground to the place where you can stand on or in your house. What was that height?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: The height of the walls was around 2 metres, and I have no idea how high the roof was. Was it 4 metres, 3 and a half metres? I'm not a builder. I really don't know, and I can't guess. I can't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me ask you this: The houses around this house, were they all the same height, were those standardised houses, all the same?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: Thank you. The whole neighbourhood had the same architecture more or less, it was the same height, it could be a difference of 20, 30 centimetres, with the exception of the newest houses which were built later according to some sort of international plan. Our houses, however, were built on old designs based on the laws of former Yugoslavia at the time. So the whole neighbourhood had to build the -- exactly the same model of the houses, that was the law, and they were of the same height.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I believe it's time for our break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We have a break now of half an hour, and we will continue at 11.00. The court officer will show you out.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Parashumti, in your statement it says that you arrived at the house of your parents on the 1st of April; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: No, on the 20th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: It's paragraph 2 of your statement of 2000. It says you arrived on the 1st of April, and first you went to see your colleague, an Albanian and his wife, and that Albanian was killed and then you decided to go to your parents' house?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Prosecution is on their feet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Gopalan.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I wonder if the witness would like a copy of his statement if reference is being made to it. I do have a hard copy to spare, or it could be called up on the screen, if necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, either you or Mr. Djurdjic can help me to find the passage to which Mr. Djurdjic is referring. I can't find it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The first page of the statement, paragraph number 2: "After the NATO bombing started on the 24th of March, we did not leave our home."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, I now have it. Thank you. Now, are you going to be asking questions about the statement, further questions? If so, it could be useful for the witness to have a copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree, but there will be other documents as well. If the witness can confirm something from the statement, I don't see why -- but anyway, it's P903. We can call it up on the screen. The Albanian version, page 1. We have it in English. We don't need the Serbian, but we need the Albanian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Can I say that I don't read the statement the way you read it with your last question. It's not saying he moved to the house on the 1st of April. I think the statement is merely speaking of a visit to the house, whereas the witness's evidence was that he moved with his parents on the 20th of April. It may be an issue of the translation, but this reference in the statement appears to be to a visit with his wife on the 1st of April to the house of a friend. It's not talking about him moving in with his parents on the 20th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, in the second paragraph of your statement you say: "After the NATO bombings started ... on the 24th, we did not leave our home." Which home do you mean?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but I did not understand you. At the beginning?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Do you see in the second paragraph of the statement in front of you -- can you read the sentence starting with "Prej fillimit."

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: That's correct, that we did not leave our home. But on the 1st I just wasn't to the Cana's home because there was a death in the family, a relative of Cana had been killed. He was a lawyer by profession. He remained -- his body remained in his yard for three days and then he was taken into the house --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: -- and buried there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: My question was about the end of this sentence, namely that you did not leave your home when the bombings started on the 24th of March. Which home -- which building do you mean when you say that?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: I mean Januz Cana's home.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, let's clear this up. You had your apartment where you explained at the exit from the town, and you had a house together with your uncle. Do you mean your apartment or your father's house when you say we did not leave our home?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: When I speak about the 24th of March, there were no movement at that time by people in the neighbourhood, and we went to this neighbour to offer our condolences, and we risked our lives to go there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: When you went to this family friend to express your condolences, you went with your wife?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I went together with my wife. He was an in-law of him. He lived in another neighbourhood. But his wife and other women in the neighbourhood went to find the body and to bury him. I don't know how he died. I know that he was killed. And for three days his body was lying in the yard. He was a very well-known person in Gjakove. He was a lawyer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I wonder whether you could help us to understand, that was on the 24th of March. On that day, where were you living with your wife?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the 24th of March, I was at my father's together with my two children. My wife and the other two children were at her parents. In fact, her father was deceased, but her mother was there; and she stayed there together with the children until the 27th. And then because part of the Cabrat neighbourhood was burned, they left the area there and came to my father's house on the 27th of March.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you for that. Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, I'm interested in this time, in the Serbian translation I've got 12.05, that is just after noon. Tell me, what time was it on the 2nd of April when you saw the police knocking on doors? That's paragraph 3: "On the 2nd of April at approximately 12.05..." Why don't you tell me what time it was?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: It was at night. 12.05 midnight. Around midnight. It was 2405 as I can express it another way.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to come back to the 1st of April when you were going back home with your wife. You were confronted by three policemen. Will you tell us what these policemen were doing. Where were they?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: Januz Cana's wife and his son saw us off up to the gate. There was also Ganimete Cana with us. And my wife saw the policemen when she was at the gate and said, There are three policemen there. And we went back. We stayed there for about several minute, maybe 4 or 5 minutes; and then Fatmir Cana said, You can go now, they won't do anything to you. He was not afraid, he was a student in France, he lived and studied in France for about ten years, he did not know what fear was. But we were afraid because we lived with fear. Fatmir went ahead of us. The three policemen stopped at my garage. There is a tree there. He took out his gun, but he did not shoot. Thank God we were able to go home and Fatmir stayed there and watched us until we got home. This is what happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I forgot to ask you before, were you employed at the time?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: No. Nothing was working at the time. No factories. There was only one tile factory that was still operational, all the others were closed down. From 1990, nothing was happening and nobody was working. Not because they didn't want to work, but because we were not allowed to work.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But before you stopped working, were you on sick leave?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: Could be. From 1981 I have been ill, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Will you tell us why you went to see a doctor?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: I suffer from prostate and my kidneys as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you take sick leave now and then, or were you in -- on sick leave for a long time beginning with 1990?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: We were not working in 1990 because everything was closed down. Nothing was being produced.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Just tell me, how long were you on sick leave?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: After 1981 up to 1990 I had health problems, and I was away from work for two or three weeks at a time. I took medication for my condition and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you continue to be ill after 1990?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: On that first of April, what time was it when you saw the policemen outside your gate?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: It was about 2.00 to 3.00 in the afternoon. 1500 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And why did you not dare approach those policemen standing outside your gate?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: We couldn't speak to them. It wasn't possible. It would be dangerous. It would be dangerous to look them in the eye, let alone speak to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Was the gate open?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: Yes. At that time, they were open. During day-time we would leave them open, at night we would close them. The whole neighbourhood did the same thing, they would lock the doors at night.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did the policemen go into your yard, into your house?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: These ones, the three on this occasion, no, no, I apologise, no, they did not enter my yard.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And did you watch them standing outside your gate all that time?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: After we went back home, we did not see them anymore, and we did not venture out. There was a garage there and that's where we saw them. When we were trying to get out of Januz Cana's house, we saw them, they were at the garage. Then we went into our yard. They were not in my yard; they were on the main road in front of the garage.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you just explain, when you come in from the street, do you come straight into the garage, the one you are talking about?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: There is a sidewalk about 3 metres wide and then you can see the gate to the garage.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And where is the entrance gate relative to the garage?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: About 1 to 1.20 metres from the garage.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: What kind of uniform were those policemen wearing?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: Blue. All three of them. They were single coloured blue.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: How far were you from them when you saw them?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: When I was going into my yard, I was about 2 metres from them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did they have any insignia on the uniforms?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: No, nothing. Just uniforms, no emblems or insignia.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And did they wear anything in terms of head-gear?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: Police caps.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: What does that police cap look like?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: The caps were similar to the military ones. The ones that they used to have before. Not the ones that the traffic police wear.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Was that the same model of the cap like the one you wore in the army?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: Yes, yes, similar. The colour was different.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell me your date of birth.

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: I was born on the 13th of August, 1955.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I now call up P904. It's already an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, this B is the house of your father; correct?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And could you mark the house --

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, will you please instruct me if I may continue using this drawing and ask the witness to make additional markings, or do you want me to take a new blank photograph for the new markings? What is better?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: A blank would be better, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Then I would like the 65 ter document 275.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you please just mark the house where you were in the evening of the 2nd of April.

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: My close family stayed in the basement of my uncle's, which is here. This is the entrance to the basement.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you please listen to what I'm asking you to do. Could you mark the house, your father's house, and put number 1 next to that one.

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And could you please put number 1 next to it, or rather, in the middle --

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: -- of the square, yes, thank you. Now, could you please mark your uncle's house with number 2.

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I would like you to mark Cana Januz's house and mark it with number 3.

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you please just put number 3 in there.

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now, I would like you to mark Naser Rudi's house.

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And could you please mark it with number 4.

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now, I would like you to mark Dardan Riza's house? Very well. And then if we look at this photograph, don't make any markings because it's not on the photograph. Where is Dardan Riza's house? It's not on the photograph, but is it to the left, to the right, behind the road, behind the houses that we can see here, on this side, or on the other side where we are?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: It's on our side some 2, 3, 4, 5, the 6th house in our direction -- house down in our direction, on our side.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So it's opposite the street behind your house, the house that belonged to your father and to your uncle, is that what you are trying to tell us?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: They are all in a row.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Well, if they are all in a row, is it then to the left or to the right?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: To the left.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Behind house number 4?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's remark: Could the speakers, please, not overlap.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. So Behar Haxhiavdia's house, do you know where that one is? Can we see it on the photograph?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: No, it is not. It's his wife's family. He lives in another neighbourhood, but his wife had sought shelter here.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Gopalan.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Please could we briefly go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now I would like you to mark Lulzim Vejsa's house.

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, could you please mark it with number 5.

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I would like to ask you to draw Dardan Riza's house.

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: In this direction to the left, but it can't be seen. It's to the left, a bit higher.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, here where you put the red line, could you please mark it with number 7.

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: But inside the photograph. And I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This black part here, will we see it on the photograph or not? Will it remain like this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We can go on then.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you please -- well, how far is this house?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] for the record, number 7 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You've already asked that, Mr. Djurdjic. The witness has told you all of this about that house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: The Krasniqi house, could you please mark that one.

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: The Krasniqi's house cannot be seen here. The Berisha's, however, can be seen, the Krasniqis are further down. Not the first, second, or -- the third one belongs to the Krasniqis. It's in this direction, but it can't be seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is this inside the photograph? I need the assistance -- I need to know that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I don't understand what you are asking, Mr. Djurdjic. You are told that the Krasniqi house is not on the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, you can see the red marking at the bottom of the photograph. I'm merely asking whether it's visible, whether it will remain visible, whether it's part of the photograph; and then we can mark it with a number or else we can just ask him to describe and tell us that this is the direction in which the Krasniqi house is. So whether this will be saved as part of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It won't be saved where he has marked. For the record, the witness has indicated the Krasniqi house is off the picture on the bottom of the photograph. So it doesn't need to be marked, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, sir, how far is your father's house from the Krasniqi house?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: It must be around 60 metres. I'm not 100 per cent certain though. 50 to 60 metres, approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now could you mark the police car that you saw. Just put a dot where that car was.

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you please make the dot a little bigger, and mark it with number 8.

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Apart from that car, while you were up there, did you see anything elsewhere that place where you were standing? I'm not talking about people.

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: No. I heard other voices, and I heard the voices of other cars -- I heard, sorry, the sound of other cars. I heard cars that made a louder noise, but I was not able to see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I would like you to mark the location where you saw three policemen with another dot.

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now, could you please put number 9 next to it. Above the dot, please.

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you tell me what uniform did those three police officers wear? What kind of uniforms?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: They wore hats. They had green uniforms on.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And were you able to see any other details on the uniforms?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: I can't remember. It was dark. It was pitch dark, and I can't remember. I remember that there were three of them. There was the flickering of the flames lasted only seconds, and then there was deep darkness. And the wind was blowing in the direction of the flames.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I would like to ask you to mark with an X very carefully the place where you were standing, but I don't want us to ruin this photograph, so could you please just mark it very neatly and carefully with an X.

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And could you please put number 10 above it. Number 10 above this X that you put in.

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Excellent. Thank you very much. Now, I would like you to tell me, I don't want us to ruin the photograph, the other people who came into your yard, where were they? Where did you see them?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: Here. Do you want me to mark it? That's the dot near that wall.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes, but please -- thank you. I don't want you to ruin the photograph. Mark it, but let's not ruin the markings that we already have. Now, Witness, I didn't see whether you marked the location where the other three policemen were or not.

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: Yes, here. Where the number 9 is.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Please, is this the second dot that you put on the left?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: To the left.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Excellent. Then mark it with number 11.

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, could you tell me, the other policemen that you marked with number 11, when you saw them did you see what colour uniforms --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Sorry, that is not policemen. The witness has said they were people. He was asked to mark where people were in his yard. Do you want him to say whether they are police or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They were policemen in uniform.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now the records tells us. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: But I wanted to ask you if you could see from the place where you were what colour uniforms they were wearing?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: Blue.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And could you please tell me, you say that you saw Dragan Shipanoviq and Nenad -- I assume it's Nenad Raqeviq and two other policemen exiting Cana's house. Can you tell me, where did they go out?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: That is true. I saw four policemen there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Gopalan.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: I'd just like to point out that the corrections that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, we know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The point of the corrections is that the witness says he is not sure about the names. He is sure there were four, but he is not sure that they were the two names that you have mentioned. He suspects it was them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I'm not interested in the names. I merely put them in for easier reference.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So these people that you saw, I'm interested in the other part. Where were they going to when they left? So these people that you say that they were policemen in Cana's yard, why did you see them? They passed through what?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: They went out together with Januz Cana's daughter. Two were holding her by the shoulders and were heaving her, and then they tore her pyjamas apart. There were two following behind, one had a torch, an electrical torch, and was showing it towards the tunnel which links to the main road. From one of the policemen, from the light of the torch one could see that one of the policemen had a knife in his hand. Then they pulled her by the hair and a scream was heard. She screamed in Serbian, she said, "You killed my father." I was not able to see her father being killed, but that's what she said, that her father had been killed. Before the entrance to the tunnel, there was this scream. However, when she went into the tunnel - and I remember because I was very scared - I really heard an awful scream, just like, you know, the screams that you get when you slaughter animals. And from that moment onwards I just descended; I was unable to stay there because I felt very scared.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, where is this tunnel on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: May I mark it? Do you want me to put a dot?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes, okay.

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And could you mark it with number 12.

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And can you tell me, the numbers marked -- the numbers 9 to 11, does this mark the wall between the yard that belonged to your uncle and your father and Cana's yard?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you have to go out into the street in order to be able to get into Cana's yard?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: Only from the main road. There is no entrance.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I beg your pardon, but did I ask about Afrim Berisha's house? To tell you the truth, I can't recall right now whether I did or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: No, you did not.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Afrim Berisha's house can be seen very, very little. It's on the side. However, Naim Berisha's house, his uncle's son, can be seen. Do you want me to mark Naim's house because Afrim's cannot be seen here in this picture. Only a little bit can be seen there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So you can't see it at all?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: You can see just a little bit. Only a little bit. Just a corner. Do you want me to mark it?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: So could you please just mark the corner.

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: No need to mark. Yes, this bit can be seen. This belongs to the uncle's house. The whole of it. Once Afrim's house cannot be seen, just a bit of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
