utterances.text: But where, where is that small part? I didn't really understand what you were saying.

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: The corner that can be seen belongs to Afrim Berisha's house, while the full house belongs to his uncle's son called Naim Berisha.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: I just don't understand what part of the picture are you referring to, to the left, to the right, up, down?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: Forgive me, but you asked about Afrim Berisha's house, and it's off the picture. I was born here and lived there, but I can't see Afrim Berisha's house there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But you told me that only a little part was visible, but if it's not visible, then it's okay. But in what direction was his house?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: I mean this one which can be seen only a little bit, to the bottom, towards the bottom of this picture. Only a tiny bit of the house can be seen there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I would like to tender this into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be assigned D00220, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we get again 65 ter 275.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, this first white house on the right-hand side, whose house was that?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: You mean this one here? Do you mean this one?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, the white house. There is a roof covering two houses. No, up there. You see the angle of the house and another house next to it.

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: Yes. This is Lulzim Vejsa's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Will you put number 1 there, please.

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And deep down behind that house we can see another house. Whose house was that?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: That was a coffee shop, a cafeteria.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Please listen to me carefully, Witness. You've just told me that a tavern was located in this house number 1?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm asking you about the house at the top of the picture, the roof of which we can see in the right-hand top corner.

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: Here, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: If you see that roof, put a mark there. To the extreme right, a large house, the top of the picture.

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: This one here?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Whose house was that?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: Lutfi Nuci's.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Put number 2 there, please.

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: What about the house right next to number 2, to whom did it belong?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: This was Lul Vejsa's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Put number 3 there, please.

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Next to number 2 on the right there is a house with a roof. Whose house was that?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: His son's house, Enver's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Please put number 4 on the roof of that house.

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: To the right we see again another roof next to number 4. Whose house was that?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: This is a long garage. It's Xhemil Caka's.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Put number 5 there, please.

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: In front of number 5, the roof that is four sided, whose house was that?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: This is Xhemil Caka's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Put number 6 there.

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: The house next to number 5, to the right, whose house was that?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: This is Fetah Kastrati's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Seven.

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And the house behind number 7?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: This is Mat Buriqi's house. He is a Montenegrin. Mato Boric.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Put number 8, please.

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And what about house -- the house behind number 7, to the right of number 5?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: The two-story house, the big one you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: This is Fetah Kastrati's brother's house, Ramiz Kastrati's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mark it with 9, please.

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now, let's move to the other side of the street. The first house in the street opposite the car, whose house was that?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: With the red-tiled roof? Two families lived there. On the left a Serb elderly woman lived there. On the right there was someone of the Roma ethnicity, and he still live there is.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Please mark the house of the Serb lady with 10, and the house of the Roma with 11.

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, let's move to your side of the street. Do you see, opposite the car, this tiled roof?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: It is between two houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: You see on your side of the street two houses one next to another, both of them have a roof. Whose houses were they?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: This is the new house of Januz Cana.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Please mark it with a 12.

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And the left one also belongs to him; right? Never mind then. Now, to the right of the tree at the entrance to your yard, there is a house with a tiled roof. What is that structure? Was that someone's house?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: This is a small building. It was a garage.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What about the house behind this large roof?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: This was a shop. It is a grocery shop.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: It's a bit deeper inside, behind the garage. If it was a grocery store, tell us.

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: This was Xhevdet Muhaxhiri's.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Mark Xhevdet's shop with 14, please.

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: Fourteen.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And the roof below 14, who was the owner?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: This is Xhevdet Muhaxhiri's house where he lived. It is his house in fact, but he lived in America. Now he lives in Gjakove.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Could you please mark it with 13.

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Now, in the right-hand-side corner of the picture we see another roof. Whose house was that?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: This is Agron Nagavci's house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, will you put number 15 there, please.

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. And what about the house at the bottom of the picture with the roof, below 15?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: Blerim Nagavci's, his brother.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Will you put number 16 there, please.

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: There are four brothers living there. Two live in the front part of the house, the other two live in the lower part of the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, when you go from 16 to the left, there is a structure with a roof on it. Was that an outhouse, or did someone live in there?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: Well, I think it was a house, the number 16 was a house, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: That's not what I asked you. You marked it already. But when you go to the left, I want to be fair and to ask you about all the houses with roofs. We see another roof, was that a residential building or an auxiliary structure, an outhouse?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: That was an auxiliary structure. They kept their food there. They did not live there.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Your Honours, I would like to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I now call up D002-5109, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: And that, Your Honours, will be assigned D00221.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, could you tell me, which uniform design did you see that night, the night of the 1st or the 2nd?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: The blue one. This one here.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Please put a circle around it, please.

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: And mark it with number 1.

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Did you see any other design?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: Yes, only three. This one here. It looks like it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: And that will be assigned D00222, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Witness, in the statement you gave in 2000 and in your corrigendum, or rather, supplemental information of the 15th March, 2002, you did not mention that anyone seized your documents; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: Can you repeat the question, please. I did not understand it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: In your 2000 statement and in the supplement you made in 2002, you did not mention that anyone asked for your documents, your IDs, and that you had to turn them over when you were leaving Djakovica; right?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: I can't remember. I know that I've told the truth and the truth is that they did not allow anyone to proceed towards Albania without handing over their documents. It could be that I did not mention it, but that is the truth, that I had to give up my document, my ID. The other documents that were in my flat, they are still there. The one that I had on me on that day, I had to give it to them because otherwise I wouldn't be allowed to go to Albania.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you Witness, I have no further questions for you. Thank you, Your Honours. I have completed my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Ms. Gopalan.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I do have some re-examination. I wonder if it's possible for the break to be taken now and for me to resume with my re-examination after, or I could begin immediately as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You expect to take more than seven or eight minutes, do you?

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Yes, I do, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will resume at 10 minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. Gopalan.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: I just have a few questions for you today before you complete your testimony. Now, sir, towards the end of the last session, Defence counsel asked you some questions about your identity documents. You said, and I quote.

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: "... I've told the truth and the truth is that they did not allow anyone to proceed to Albania without handing over their documents." Sir, when you said "they did not allow anyone to proceed to Albania," who were you referring to when you say "they"?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: They means the two policemen who were stationed at that little building that looked like a small shop.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Now, I'd like to ask you some questions about the three policemen you were confronted by. You spoke about this in your testimony today at page 33. You say that Januz Cana's wife and his son saw you off to the gate, and that his son -- sorry, her son, Fatmir Cana was not afraid but "We were afraid because we lived with fear." Could you explain to us what you meant when you said you were afraid because you lived with fear? What were you afraid of?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: We were afraid of the police. The uniform instilled terror.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And why is that, sir?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: If you were not somebody in their eyes, they could play around with you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And what do you mean by "play around with you"?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: We were afraid that should we not stop, they would kill us.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Now, on that evening, what happened to Fatmir Cana, if you know?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: That day in the evening, in the late hours of the evening, it might have been 1.40, 1.45, when I heard gun-shots coming from within his house. I couldn't see anything. Everybody heard the gun-shots, not only me. Throughout the neighbourhood we were able to hear shooting.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Now, do you know what happened to Fatmir Cana? If you don't, we can move on.

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: I don't know anything. I know that he is not alive, but I did not see anything. I didn't see what happened to Fatmir or Januz or Ganimete, the only thing I know is what befell Shpresa.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Now you mentioned Januz and Gamimete, could you remind us who they are, Januz and Ganimete?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: Januz was the head of the household, a teacher by profession. Ganimete was his wife. Shpresa is the eldest daughter, Fatmir being their son.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Now, after the incident in April that you described, did you see Januz and Ganimete again?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: I saw Januz in the evening when I knocked on the door to ask him to leave the house. Because by that time police cars were being -- were audible and police started emerging in the main road even though they had not started coming into our yards. And I told them to leave the house. Januz emerged from the window to say he would not abandon his house, if people were to come they would be welcome, I haven't done anything to anybody.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Now, when you returned to your neighbourhood in June, did you see Januz and Ganimete again?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: I returned on the 25th of June. We arrived late in the evening, in the afternoon, in the evening. However, the next day on the 26th we were unable to get into the Vejsa's because of the foul smell, but we were unable to see anything. We got in, but we saw a charred house. And the whole house, every room was full of tiles because the beams had burned down and everything had collapsed. I haven't seen anything with my own eyes, but I heard there were two bodies found inside. I heard that the bodies had been retrieved before the 25th, but I don't know -- two of them -- two of those bodies were inside the room. People were able to see them, but I myself never saw any bodies. That's the truth.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Now, just to clarify your answer, I would like to ask you about Januz and Ganimete specifically. I think you testified earlier that they were your neighbours. Did you see your neighbours in their home after you returned to your neighbourhood? So this was in June.

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: No, no, I did not. Neither did I see them alive, nor did I see their bodies. I saw their grave-site though, the grave of the four family members.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And where was this grave-site of the four family members?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: Their grave-site was near --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that I was patient enough regarding Ganimete and Januz. The witness responded, he said everything, and now we go back to the beginning and the witness said that he didn't know. I think that the question -- that the answers were quite specific and I -- nothing in my cross-examination has given rise to this kind of re-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The last point, Ms. Gopalan.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: I would simply refer counsel to page 33, I believe, where reference is made to the events that took place in the Cana household where the individuals I've asked about were mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The point is that the questioning in cross-examination does not warrant you going now into this extended evidence about these people. Is there something you would like to put about that?

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Simply that I can stop at this stage, Your Honours. I believe that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very good, that will be a satisfactory response.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Sir, you were also asked some questions about the -- your neighbourhood, and you marked a number of locations on the neighbourhood, if you recall. Do you remember making those markings on the photographs that set out your neighbourhood?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you. If you know, sir, based on the condition of the houses on that photograph that you saw, are you able to tell us when that photograph is from, if you know?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: Up until the 2nd of March, the whole neighbourhood was intact. However, these pictures are ones which I haven't seen before. I saw them only today for the first time, but that's reality. Everything was burned down.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: And what was it that happened on the 2nd of March up to which the neighbourhood was intact?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: The 2nd of March?

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: It could be a mistranslation. Let me just read out what the transcript says. It says: "Up until the 2nd of March, the whole neighbourhood was intact." Is that what you said? Is March correct?

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: The neighbourhood was intact on the 2nd of March, but from the 1st or the 2nd of April, things changed and that's where the change occurred throughout the neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have no further questions for the witness but one issue to raise with you. An exhibit that was marked during testimony today does not seem to reflect the full markings made by the witness, and with your leave, I would like to call up the exhibit again so that the complete marking can be reflected in the document that was tendered into evidence. I'm referring to P905 where the marking E which related to the vehicle that Your Honours requested to be marked has been omitted from the admitted exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Could I call up --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It's on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Sir, I would like you to make a marking on the photograph on the screen before you. You've already made this marking before, but it wasn't captured correctly. Now, I believe you placed an E in the past to where --

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: -- you identified the location of the vehicle that you saw. Could you please place an E to mark the location of the vehicle that you saw.

utterances.speaker: SAMI PARASHUMTI
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Could you please mark an E in that location as well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Do you now tender that --

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: Yes, please, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: -- in that completed form? It will be received. It will be received as Exhibit P905, so that it is complete. Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I don't want you to be too strict but perhaps I -- I didn't mark it correctly or I didn't note it down correctly. I thought it was P905, that's what I noted down and not 904 because in 904 I have A, B, C and in the other one I have D, and E. If that could be checked. I don't have any objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We are in complete agreement, Mr. Djurdjic. We've just corrected Exhibit P905. Sir, you'll be pleased to know that that concludes the questions for you. The Chamber would like to thank you for being able to come to The Hague and for the assistance that you have been able to give. We will be looking at this in due course when we've finished all the evidence, but we are grateful for the patience that you have shown and the assistance you've provided. You may, of course, now return to your normal activities and the court officer will show you out.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Are you taking the next witness, Ms. Gopalan?

utterances.speaker: MS. GOPALAN
utterances.text: I'm not, Your Honours. The next witness will be taken by Ms. D'Ascoli.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Your Honours, the next witness is Mr. Beqir Krasniqi, and his evidence relates to paragraph 25 to 32 of the indictment. And I think he is ready and can be brought in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Do you solemnly declare that the evidence you will give will be the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Would you please sit down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Ms. D'Ascoli, you have some questions for Mr. Krasniqi?

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Good morning, witness.

utterances.speaker: BEQIR KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Could you please state your full name for the record.

utterances.speaker: BEQIR KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes, I am Beqir Krasniqi.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. And could you also state your date and place of birth, please?

utterances.speaker: BEQIR KRASNIQI
utterances.text: I was born in 1939, on the 5th of January. I was born in Pusto Selo.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Where are you currently living?

utterances.speaker: BEQIR KRASNIQI
utterances.text: I live in Pusto Selo.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: What do you do, what is your occupation?

utterances.speaker: BEQIR KRASNIQI
utterances.text: I am a farmer.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Mr. Krasniqi, yesterday during proofing, you indicated sometimes you have difficulty understanding proper Albanian when spoken fast or with complex words. So I would please ask you, just interrupt me and ask me to repeat or to go slower if you feel that you haven't understood something, and the same applies for the Albanian translation that you hear, if there's any problem with that, please just let us know. Okay. Mr. Krasniqi --

utterances.speaker: BEQIR KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Did you provide a statement to the Office of the Prosecutor of this Tribunal in January 2000?

utterances.speaker: BEQIR KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And did you also provide a second statement to the Office of the Prosecutor of this Tribunal in May 2008?

utterances.speaker: BEQIR KRASNIQI
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Did you have the opportunity to review both statements recently; were these statements read back to you?

utterances.speaker: BEQIR KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And I understand you wanted to make some corrections to this statement. So I will take you through these corrections. Okay? And I can start with the statement of 2000 which is the 65 ter number 05136. Mr. Krasniqi, at page 3 --

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And for the record this is in both versions in the English and the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: You indicated that you have a problem with what is described in paragraph 5, in particular with the colours of the uniforms mentioned there. Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: BEQIR KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And can you -- are you able to tell the Court what the problem is with regard to this paragraph and the colours?

utterances.speaker: BEQIR KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Well, I don't -- I'm not able to show you the colours. I cannot see them very well. But if you can show me them, I can point them out.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: What do you mean --

utterances.speaker: BEQIR KRASNIQI
utterances.text: I cannot name them very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Okay. So the problem is with the name of colours or with the colours as you see them?

utterances.speaker: BEQIR KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes, exactly. I can point them out if I see them.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Okay. So you are able to recognise colours, but you have difficulties --

utterances.speaker: BEQIR KRASNIQI
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Okay. And you have difficulties with what?

utterances.speaker: BEQIR KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes, I am able.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Okay. Because -- if I can help you, in proofing you indicated to me that you have trouble understanding, for example, the meaning of the words blue or green that were mentioned in that part of the statement; is that correct? Is that the problem?

utterances.speaker: BEQIR KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: I see my learned colleague on his feet, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I don't understand this examination about the circumstances of the proofing. I simply don't understand. To my mind it would be better to admit the statement into evidence and then to ask the questions about it to clarify. Now the witness is being asked questions that relate to the proofing session, and then he is providing answers.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: May I reply, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You may, Ms. D'Ascoli.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I'm going to do, but when the witness was reviewing the statement, he had had a problem specifically with this paragraph. I felt it was fair to point it out; and I'm later going, of course, like, into the proper questioning. And I will show some photographs to him to overcome this problem. But I felt I had to address this issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The Chamber has noted that the witness is not satisfied that the paragraph reflects his true understanding, and it's to do with the colours that are shown of uniforms and that this may be partly to do with his visual recognition and partly to do with the language difficulty of which we've been aware in this trial about the colours blue and green. Now so far that's what we know.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Thank you. I can move on.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, there are then a number of small corrections that you made, and I will just -- in order to save time, I will read them and ask to confirm the corrections. Okay. At page 4, paragraph 7, for the record. Do you remember there's a sentence which says: "I gave the money to my uncle." And you said that it was Tahir who gave the money to your uncle; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BEQIR KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Okay. In the same paragraph there is a sentence which mentions Ali: "... Ali, happened to know one of the Serbs who was a policeman from Klina. The person from Klina knows the name of the policeman?" Is that correct that you indicated that you didn't know whether in fact this person from Klina knew the name of the policeman? Is that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: BEQIR KRASNIQI
utterances.text: I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Same paragraph, last sentence: "Ali left us and went in the direction where the women and children had gone." Sir, is it correct that you indicated that you don't remember about Ali going away? That's correct. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Okay. The last point, it's at page 6, paragraph 5, you indicated that your uncle Hadji Jemin Krasniqi was 88 years old, and not 84 as indicated; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: You said that he was 88 years old. 84 is what is written in the statement, sir, which is the correct one?

utterances.speaker: BEQIR KRASNIQI
utterances.text: He was 88 years old on the night when he was killed.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, briefly, the second statement, this is from May 2008, and it's the 65 ter number 05137.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: First of all, there's just a material error, Your Honours, this is at page 2, paragraph 3. The date of the end of the paragraph should be the 31st of March, 1999 clearly, not 2008. This is just a material error.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Then page 3, paragraph 12, Mr. Krasniqi, this paragraph says that you believe Ali knew the police officer because he was released unlike all others. Now, Mr. Krasniqi, you indicated that this sentence "he was released unlike all others" refers to the fact that you heard the Serbian police officer telling Ali to go away -- just a second, let me finish. But you did not know and you did not pay attention to whether he actually left or not; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BEQIR KRASNIQI
utterances.text: I did not see him because we had to look down and that's the truth.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. The very last point at page 3, paragraph --

utterances.speaker: BEQIR KRASNIQI
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. At page 3, paragraph 24, you said that you do not remember exactly how the weapon AK-47 looks like; is that correct? Is that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: BEQIR KRASNIQI
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Krasniqi, with these corrections that we now made to your statement, are you satisfied that the information in these statements is true and accurate to the best of your knowledge and belief?

utterances.speaker: BEQIR KRASNIQI
utterances.text: To the best of my knowledge and understanding, yes, because I saw things with my own eyes. I was there for three hours when all those things happened.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Your Honours, now I'd like to tender into evidence both the witness statements, please. And the statement of the year 2000 is the 65 ter number 05136.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: And that will be assigned P00908, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Thank you. And the statement from 2008 is 65 ter number 05137.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: And that will be assigned P00909, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: I can now provide a summary of this witness evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: The witness is from the village of Pusto Selo in the Orahovac municipality where he has lived for most of his live. He testifies about the attack by Serb forces on Pusto Selo on the 31st of March, 1999. On 26 March 1999 many people fled to the witness village from different places. The fleeing people stayed with the villagers of Pusto Selo in their houses. Some stayed also in the local school and the witness had about twenty people from Petkovic and Mirusa staying with him. The fleeing people told the witness that they were forced by Serb forces to leave their houses and to go to Pusto Selo. On the 31st of March, 1999, Serb forces entered Pusto Selo. The witness and other people fled only to find themselves surrounded by Serb tanks. The Serb forces approached the fleeing group and ordered them to separate men from women and children. Women and children were told then to give away their valuables and go to Albania. The men were gathered together by Serb forces and then brought close to a brook. There those Serb forces opened fire on those men and executed them. The witness was amongst those men, and he managed to survive by falling into the brook. Some bodies fell on him. The witness describes the circumstances surrounding the massacre. Several of his male relatives died in that massacre. The witness helped with the burial of bodies on the first days of April 1999. He states that they buried in Pusto Selo 106 bodies of men aged between 16 and 90. And this is the end of the in-court summary, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, I now have some questions for you related to these events in Pusto Selo in the end of March 1999. Mr. Krasniqi, in your statement of 2000 at pages 3 to 5 when you describe in detail the circumstances in which the massacre of the 31st of March occurred, you always refer to or use the expression "the Serbs." Mr. Krasniqi, can you please tell us to whom you refer by saying "the Serbs"?

utterances.speaker: BEQIR KRASNIQI
utterances.text: I mean the police.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And who were the perpetrators of the massacre you describe?

utterances.speaker: BEQIR KRASNIQI
utterances.text: The massacre was committed -- those ones who were in uniform. They were all policemen. There were about 40 of them or more. They were 20, 22 years old, and even older.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. And, Mr. Krasniqi, will you be able to identify on photographs the uniforms of the Serb forces that you saw in Pusto Selo on the 31st of March, 1999?

utterances.speaker: BEQIR KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness be asked to sit closer to the microphones. We can hardly hear him.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, would you mind sitting a little bit closer to the microphones, please. Thank you. That's better.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: I'm going to show you some photographs, Mr. Krasniqi. Can I please have on the screen the Exhibit number P831?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, are you able to see the pictures on the video?

utterances.speaker: BEQIR KRASNIQI
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Okay. That's good. Is any --

utterances.speaker: BEQIR KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes, I can. This one here --

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: You recognise it already. Just a second.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Maybe could the usher provide him with a pen. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Could you mark --

utterances.speaker: BEQIR KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes, please. I don't know how to write though.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Just a mark, just whatever. But can you please --

utterances.speaker: BEQIR KRASNIQI
utterances.text: I'm illiterate.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: -- can you please answer a question? Just before that, can you answer a question? Is any of these colours, or any of these patterns, is any of these similar to the colours or the uniforms that you saw in Pusto Selo on the 31st of March?

utterances.speaker: BEQIR KRASNIQI
utterances.text: This one, yes, but the ones that were at the school, I did not see them. I saw the ones that were close to us, but not the ones that were at the school.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: No, no, of course. Let's just talk about what you saw and the forces that you saw at any point during the day and before the massacre. So you said that some -- like, one of -- or some of these pictures are similar to uniforms that you saw. Could you mark with any sign the picture that you think -- or the pictures that you think are similar to what -- to the uniforms that you saw in Pusto Selo at the end of March 1999?

utterances.speaker: BEQIR KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Here? Can I mark here?

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Yes, please. Perfect. That's okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Your Honours, can I please tender this exhibit into evidence as marked by the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be assigned P00910, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And can I please call the exhibit number -- the 65 ter number 02586. Can we enlarge the picture, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, again, if you can please look at these men in uniforms, and can you tell me if any of these men are wearing the same uniforms that you saw when -- just before the massacre or anyway when you were there in Pusto Selo on the 31st of March, 1999, and you -- sorry, if you can indicate whether you recognised any of these uniforms as the same one that you saw on that day of the massacre?

utterances.speaker: BEQIR KRASNIQI
utterances.text: I cannot say anything about these. I don't recognise these.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: You don't recognise the colours and the uniforms of these men?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The witness has answered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: No, he hasn't, Mr. Djurdjic. His answer was unclear, and it's being corrected to clarify it. Carry on please, Ms. D'Ascoli.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, I'm not talking about these gentlemen here in the pictures. I'm just asking you whether you are able to recognise the colours and the type of uniforms that they are wearing. Just the uniforms that they have and whether any of these uniforms reminds you of the ones of the perpetrators of the massacre in Pusto Selo on the 31st of March? Which is your answer, Mr. Krasniqi?

utterances.speaker: BEQIR KRASNIQI
utterances.text: I'm not sure about these. I cannot tell them apart. I think the other ones were lighter.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: What do you mean by "the other ones were lighter"?

utterances.speaker: BEQIR KRASNIQI
utterances.text: I don't understand. I am sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Okay. No problem. I will try to be simpler. Can you see well the pictures on the screen?

utterances.speaker: BEQIR KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Can you distinguish these four men in uniforms?

utterances.speaker: BEQIR KRASNIQI
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And I'm not concerned about, you know, their faces, but only about what they are wearing. Okay?

utterances.speaker: BEQIR KRASNIQI
utterances.text: The clothes they are wearing.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Exactly. I'm just concerned about that, exactly. Now, if you can think about the uniforms or the Serb forces that you saw doing the massacre, the perpetrators of the massacre in Pusto Selo; so if you can think about those, what you remember, and if you can tell me whether what they were wearing matches what is in the picture, any of these four men.

utterances.speaker: BEQIR KRASNIQI
utterances.text: Well, I don't understand. I can see what they are wearing, but I don't know what you mean by distinguishing them. And if you want me to show what kind of clothes they are wearing, I can tell you. But otherwise I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: I am sorry, I was just meaning whether what you see here in the picture looks like what you saw in Pusto Selo on those men, on the Serb forces, who were the perpetrators of the massacre, that's what I mean. If you can help us with that, otherwise we move forward, there's no problem.

utterances.speaker: BEQIR KRASNIQI
utterances.text: They are not the same. They are not the same.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Okay. Maybe I can show you a simpler picture.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think we've run out of time, Ms. D'Ascoli.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Yeah, that's right. Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Krasniqi, we have to stop now because of the time, and we continue -- we continue on Monday. An officer of the court will assist you over the break and will arrange for you to be back with us on Monday when we will continue with your evidence and hear what you need to say.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Sorry about the interruption, but we have limited hours that we can use this courtroom. So we must now adjourn, and we continue on Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 15th of June, 2009, at 12.00 p.m.
